reality_delta: No new hook-quality artifact exists yet. The bounded bundle only contains pre-existing files (advisory_stop.py, codex-hook.py, check_runner.py, advisory-stop.json, redcap). The proposal is still a plan; no contract, module, wired check, or executed sample replay has been produced. Reality has not changed.
main_concern: The design proposal describes the right shape (contract + four sample classes + aggregate check + Prism-reviewed threshold changes) but omits the concrete contents that would make it a real measurement. Without specified sample definitions, threshold values, and trend computation rules, implementation can easily become a metrics theater that produces passing reports without measuring actual hook behavior.
top_risks: Sample sets may be synthetic and disconnected from real events recorded by codex-hook.py, making false-positive/false-negative rates unrepresentative.
Threshold values could be chosen after the fact to guarantee passage rather than derived from a real quality target, violating the 'no silent relaxation' constraint.
The 'trend threshold' concept is undefined (window size, aggregation rule, failure condition), inviting a no-op or moving-target implementation.
missing_evidence: Draft content of assets/contracts/hook-quality-metrics.json showing concrete samples for all four classes and explicit numeric thresholds with rationale.
Mapping from recorded host-hook events (codex-hook.py) to sample classes, proving the samples are grounded in actual hook history.
Implementation sketch of runtime/core/hook_quality_metrics.py demonstrating that an injected false-positive sample and an injected false-negative high-risk sample each cause the report to fail.
minimum_fix: Before writing runtime code, produce a draft contract with at least one concrete sample per class, explicit threshold values and their derivation, a precise trend rule (window + failure condition), and a documented sample refresh cadence from real hook events. Require a Prism re-review of that draft before implementation begins.

anti_loop_signal.reason: Adding a new contract and a new check can create the illusion that RSP-25 is 'covered'. Treat RSP-25 as open until the check is executed and observed to fail on injected false-positive and false-negative probes, then pass after the underlying hook behavior is corrected.

user_intent_alignment: The design direction matches the user's intent: move from case-by-case hook fixes to continuous false-positive/false-negative measurement. However, the user asked for implementation, and the current deliverable is only a plan. It must not be reported as completion of RSP-25.
